summary: This step merges the four lanes into one consensus ranking using RRF (reciprocal rank fusion, a way to combine several ranked lists by summing each item's 1/rank across every list it appears in, so a list that never ranks an item contributes nothing to it). Two runs were made: catalogue-free (AlphaMissense, ESM1b, SpliceAI) puts the confirmed pair at rank 20,639 of 52,012, fused score 0.000083; adding REVEL moves it only to 21,497 of 52,219, an 858-place shift with an identical fused score. The fused score for the catalogue-free run is exactly 1/(60 + 11,980) — SpliceAI's own reciprocal rank and nothing else — because AlphaMissense, ESM1b and REVEL each abstain rather than vote, having scored only one of the pair's two alleles. The cross-lane agreement matrix shows two blocks: the three missense lanes correlate at +0.168 to +0.580 with each other, while SpliceAI's correlation with any of them stays near zero (+0.021 to +0.043) — one opinion sampled three ways, plus one unrelated opinion. All 90 disagreement rows share the same shape: a splice-window allele a missense model finds unremarkable.
why: A merged ranking is only trustworthy if a reader can tell a low fused rank apart from three lanes actively voting it down — otherwise the report would misreport structural blindness (a lane that cannot see the pair's consequence class) as a genuine scientific disagreement about how damaging the pair is. Running both a catalogue-free and an all-lanes fusion, and checking the ablation's effect on rank, is what lets this step show the REVEL catalogue lane is not doing the work: excluding it barely moves the rank and leaves the fused score bit-for-bit identical.
verdict: H064 (`P4-8`) refuted: the catalogue-free RRF consensus ranks the confirmed pair 20,639 of 52,012, far from the predicted rank 1. The refutation's cause is abstention, not disagreement — three of four lanes have no rank to contribute because each scored only one allele of a half-nonsense pair, a lane-coverage gap step 1 and step 2 predicted before any ranking ran. The step also verified the RRF method's own citation (Crossref confirms the DOI, three authors, SIGIR 2009, pages 758-759), so the refutation is not attributable to a wrong or unverifiable fusion formula.

inherits.what: The agreement matrix and RRF fusion both need every lane's per-pair rank and per-allele score already computed and captioned in step 5 — this step reuses step 5's allele-level finding (three lanes independently rank the missense allele in their own top 2.6%) to explain why the pair-level fusion result is abstention rather than genuine disagreement, rather than re-deriving that explanation from scratch.

hands_to.what: Nothing in iteration 4 reads step 6's output — it is the terminal step of the chain that ran (step 7, Track 2's graph walk, has not run). Its refutation and its abstention-not-disagreement explanation are instead the finding iteration 4 hands to Track 1's report: a compound-heterozygous zoo consensus is silent on the confirmed pair not because the models disagree with the clinical case, but because the roster is missense-heavy and the pair is half nonsense — the gap GPN-MSA's still-pending promotion (recorded since step 1) would close.
